title: The Grain Road
timelinePosition: Directly after Chapter 4, with the party riding southwest from the sick village toward the source.
openLocation: Lordaeron trade roads between village depots and the routes feeding into Andorhal.
immediateObjective: Work backward along the grain trail until they find the road that holds the whole plague network together.
constraints: Limited third, absolute: Sylvanas only. Nothing she cannot see, hear, read or infer.

Elves cannot feel the contamination. Every reading of exposure arrives through Jaina (spell light, staff, her marks on the map). Sylvanas sees the result and the mage's face, never the sickness itself.
Narration: Sylvanas thinks 'the mage' until Beat 7, where she catches herself thinking 'Jaina' and lets it stand. Not before. Aloud it stays 'Mage' (or 'Proudmoore' in front of others) all chapter.
No warmth. Their trust is work-first. Respect is practical: she uses Jaina's read to choose the road.
Jaina's hands: left raw and wrapped, right dead since Ch2; hand-reading is banned. Readings go through spell light and the staff.
The overseer lies, is alive, and is gone when they return. Never bring him back after Beat 6.
The Barov name is proof of connection, not guilt. Sylvanas refuses to blur that line, and the narration must not blur it either.

The old carter is a nagging memory only. No proof, no pattern. Jaina does not pre-empt the snag; it is Sylvanas's alone. He must not be identified with or as the young grain-man with the cart. His one link to that man is that he asked after him, and that stays a question.
No Mal'Ganis naming. No Kel'Thuzad naming. No certainty about who designed the plague.
No counted time in dialogue ('two breaths'). Orders by event.
Grain-as-loud-carrier is established (Ch4). Do not re-prove it; the chapter is about scale and the road, not about the sickroom. Register is paper, records, road, not another sickroom.
Neral and the fourth ranger are gone; the two empty places in the line are a callback, not a new image.
Neral stays on the northbound warning line. Do not bring her back.
Cyndia must have a real function (counting, records, perimeter reads) before her Ch10 shift. She has been thin for two chapters.
Lyriel rides at Jaina's knee when the road allows and jokes where Cyndia won't. She calls Jaina 'Jaina' (Ch4 landed this).
Do not name the village from Ch4 unless the Ch4 final does. It is unnamed on the page; refer to it as the village / the one with the granary fire.

Timeline and the rut read: the last rain fell before dawn on the morning they left the village (Ch4). No new rain on the page until after B6, or the rut read breaks. The overseer's 'two days ago' must fall after that rain (see timeAnchor on B4-B6).

Jaina's marks: the right hand is dead and only two fingertips of the wrapped left hand work (Ch4). Her marks on the map go down clumsily with those two fingers, or another hand makes them at her word (Tobin's slate in Ch4 is the precedent). 'Ink-stained fingers' belong to clerks, Sylvanas or Cyndia, not to Jaina.

Arthas and Strahnbrad are new on the page. Sylvanas needs an on-page source for the army being at Strahnbrad before B9: road talk from the S1 innkeepers and merchants, or the B6 toll-keeper. The writer picks one.
Cyndia's turned head after the carter's wagon (Ch3) belongs to Ch9 and Ch15. Nobody raises it in Ch5, and Sylvanas does not ask Cyndia about the carter.

povKnowsAtOpen: Someone organized the wagons and is killing loose ends.
The trail points southwest toward Andorhal (ANDORHAL stencil on the sacking, folded in her coat; Brask: three days by cart down the grain road; everything in the south goes through it).
Most towns are only in the early stage of the sickness, but Millhaven was hit hard.
They stopped the grain in time at the sick village, and it lives.
Jaina can read contamination before other people know a place is sick.

The girl's 'newer grain seller' at Millhaven and the sick village's young man with the cart are, she and Jaina judged in Ch4, one man. The old carter on the Millhaven road asked after a young grain man too. That question is the carter's only thread to anything, and it proves nothing.
A watcher was placed in the granary, carried poison sewn into his collar and died rather than talk (Ch4): the network is organized and wastes its people.
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: Who is really running the trade route.
Whether the Barovs built the plague, helped cover it, or know nothing.
Whether the old carter matters or just looks suspicious in hindsight.
mustNotBeImpliedYet: No certainty that the Barovs are guilty.
No sudden warmth between Sylvanas and Jaina.
No proof that the old carter is the creature behind the plague.
castKnowsLeavingChapter: A live regional network is moving grain and cleaning the road ahead of them; they arrive after each move.
Andorhal is the hub the routes pinch toward.
The Barov name is all over the grain paper: connection, not proven guilt.
The depot overseer lied; it cost them a day; he is alive and gone.
The southern supply road is the best approach and runs straight through Arthas's war near Strahnbrad.
Sylvanas carries the old carter forward as a nagging memory, unmatched to anything.
Arthas's army is at work near Strahnbrad against the orcs (from road talk or the toll-keeper); Sylvanas expects it to rank the grain below the orcs.

pov: She starts the ride treating this like road work: map the depots, read the wagons, find the break in the trail.
The records get too big and too strange for tracking alone, and she has to lean on Jaina's magic to keep the hunt moving.
The overseer's lie costs them a day. Sylvanas reads it from the road, a day late.
By the end, Sylvanas is no longer just tolerating Jaina's help. She is using Jaina's read to choose the road ahead.

beats: Sylvanas opens still half-expecting theory and softness from Jaina.
Jaina keeps matching the work: fast reads, quick corrections, no pride when the facts change.
Sylvanas's respect turns practical. She stops thinking the mage and starts thinking Jaina.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They start out doing the same job from different angles, still sharp with each other.
The miles force a clean split of labor: Jaina finds the invisible trail, Sylvanas follows the paper and the road.
By the end, they are still not gentle, but they are finally trusting the same hunt.

castAndHandoffRules.Lyriel: Still riding point and perimeter. When the road allows she rides at Jaina's knee, and she jokes where Cyndia won't.
castAndHandoffRules.Depot overseer: Alive. He lies to them and is gone when they come back. Do not bring him back.
castAndHandoffRules.Neral: Not with the party. She stays on the northbound warning line.
castAndHandoffRules.nextChapterStarts: Chapter 6 opens with the same four riders on the southern road, heading toward the military zone near Strahnbrad before Andorhal.

chapterBridge.previousChapterClose: Ch4 ends in Jaina's POV at the dawn after the rain: the village lives, Brask writes their names in his ledger, Sylvanas shows the ANDORHAL square cut from the loft sacks and folds it back into her coat ('Either way, it's the road he drove'), and the four ride down through the village in crest order with two empty places at the back. At the split past the brook the staff leans toward the ruts, and Sylvanas turns onto the grain road without a word.
chapterBridge.continuityOfState: Same day, hours later, same four riders in the same order. Jaina is spent from the all-night ward vigil: hands wrapped, left palm split and rebound, right dead, staff in the crook of the dead arm, reads by staff only. Sylvanas carries the sacking square, has Tam's teeth marks in two bare fingers, and her left glove is still grey with flour. The Ch4 win is behind them; the network that wastes its watchers is ahead.
chapterBridge.informationAsymmetry: First time inside Sylvanas since Ch3. She saw Jaina's dusk report, the shell, the wards that held, Tam die. She does not know Jaina's private guilt over Tam, that Jaina now thinks 'Sylvanas', or that Jaina doubts the stencil more than she said. Jaina still does not know about Sylvanas's palm on the stone or the circle on the map.
chapterBridge.orientingAnchor: One anchor is enough: the folded square in her coat, or the deep ruts of the grain road. Do not re-run the village.
chapterBridge.intentionalJump: POV switch from Jaina to Sylvanas, with a short time skip inside the same day (village gate to the first depot office).

scene.title: The South Road
scene.sceneFunction: They lock the route to Andorhal, Sylvanas fully accepts Jaina as a working partner, and the old carter clue comes back.
scene.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Day 4, night. They have the Barov name, Andorhal as the hub, and a road being cleaned ahead of them. A day is lost. Sylvanas has owned the overseer error to herself and refused to turn the name into a verdict.

beats.goal: At a midnight stop, fuse the paper trail with Jaina's magical map into one working picture of the network and its roads.
beats.conflict: Too much paper, a day lost, tired hands, and Sylvanas's own habit of waiting for the mage to need handling before she will rely on her.

outcome.summary: The road pattern snaps into place. Jaina gives hard, useful answers without needing to be handled. Sylvanas catches herself thinking 'Jaina' and lets it stand. The read she now trusts is the one B9 turns into a road.

beats.valueShift: holding her at arm's length -> using her read
newOnPageInformation: The paper trail and Jaina's magical map fit into one pattern of roads
Jaina's reads are hard and useful and need no handling
The routes converge on Andorhal as the hub
stillUnknownAfterBeat: What the Barov connection really means
sensoryAnchors: Cyndia and Lyriel outside the perimeter
quiet concentration instead of another argument
cold night air at the door
beats.interiority: no handling needed, which is rare in a human mage and rarer in a Kirin Tor one; catches herself thinking the name and lets it stand; work, and only work; still half-waiting for the softness, and annoyed it hasn't come
beats.plannerWarning: First on-page 'Jaina' in Sylvanas's head. Narration changes from 'the mage' to 'Jaina' here and stays changed afterward. Dialogue still 'Mage'. Do not announce the change; let it land in the narration and do not comment on it beyond the Inside line.
beats.transitionIntent: emotional carryover: the pattern now looks deliberate, and a deliberate pattern makes one odd old man on the Millhaven road sit wrong.
beats.timeAnchor: Night of day 4: the midnight stop, south of the depot.
beats.continuityNote: Ch4 left them a working pair with a shared win and no warmth; Jaina already thinks 'Sylvanas' (Sylvanas does not know). This beat is the matching hinge on Sylvanas's side, internal only. Aloud: 'Mage'. No thanks, no softening, no shared look given weight.

beats.emotion: Irritation at a memory she cannot make into anything.
beats.dilemma: Treat the old carter as one odd man on a road, as she has told rangers a hundred times, or as the first piece of a pattern she cannot prove.
beats.decision: She files him as a memory, not a pattern, and carries him forward without pretending he is proof.
beats.valueShift: clean certainty about the network -> an unplaced snag
newOnPageInformation: The old carter from the Millhaven road comes back to her: his empty wagon, his question about the grain-man
The operation is too controlled for the encounter to sit easily
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Why the old carter keeps bothering her
How the depot knew to expect them
sensoryAnchors: grain dust on old wagon boards
the echo of a polite flat voice
the irritation of missing something important
beats.interiority: one odd old man on a road, and she has told rangers a hundred times that one is nothing; then why him; an empty wagon going home empty; the depot knew to expect them, and who told it; irritated at a memory she can't make into anything
beats.plannerWarning: The carter is observable-only. Do not have Sylvanas decide what he is, and do not have Jaina or Cyndia raise him. Correct handles from the Ch3 page: an empty wagon ('Empty going up, full coming down', her own thought then); 'Nothing for me here, then', after which he drove on north, up the empty street into the dead village rather than turning for home; his question after a young fellow with a grain cart, 'coming down from your way'; 'well enough on market day' against five days dead. Do not conflate him with the young man with the cart.
beats.transitionIntent: emotional carryover: the nagging memory rides with her into the choice of road.
beats.timeAnchor: Same night, after the map settles.
beats.continuityNote: Earlier plan text said the wagon was 'heading away from Millhaven'. On the page it drove north, deeper into the dead village. Use the page. Guard the Ch3 plant: Lyriel told the carter they would watch for the grain man going south. Sylvanas may set the carter beside the unanswered 'who told the depot' in the same quiet, but she must not draw the line from Lyriel's answer to the leak. That link is for a second reading, not for her. If the farewell words recur, they recur only in her own head; Cyndia's corroboration belongs to Ch9.

beats.dilemma: The main highway is the open way and the one a watched road would predict; the southern supply road is the best path but runs straight through Arthas's war near Strahnbrad.
beats.decision: They choose the southern supply road into Andorhal, off the main highway. The choice rests on Jaina's read from B7: Sylvanas takes it without asking for proof, which is the arc landing. She warns Jaina what the army will do: pour its strength into the orcs it can already see and rank the poisoned grain below them.
beats.valueShift: open choice -> committed road, through the army
newOnPageInformation: The southern supply road is the only workable approach and forces them through human military traffic
Jaina's read is what tips the choice of road
An encounter with Arthas is now unavoidable
Sylvanas expects the army to rank the grain below the orcs
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether Arthas will listen, help, or get in their way
sensoryAnchors: a knife pinning the map at Strahnbrad
horses turning south into distant army dust
beats.interiority: the road she would pick if she were hunting them, which means it may be the road they watch; no better one; the army will look at the orcs and not at the bread
beats.plannerWarning: Do not stage Arthas on page; the army is dust and the warning is Sylvanas's prediction, delivered as a plain assessment, not a speech. Chapter 6 opens with the ride into the zone.
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: the horses turn south, and Chapter 6 opens on the ride into the military zone.
beats.continuityNote: Arthas is named on the page for the first time in the book. Sylvanas's knowledge that his army is at Strahnbrad needs an earlier source in this chapter (S1 road talk or the B6 toll-keeper). He is dust and rumour only; no on-page staging. The highway-as-watched-road logic follows from B4 (the road is being watched).

factsLocked: The party is on the southern road toward Andorhal.
Their chosen road runs through Arthas's military zone near Strahnbrad.
The Barov name keeps appearing in the grain records, but guilt is still unproven.
They lost a day to the overseer's lie.
The old carter is a nagging memory for Sylvanas, not yet a pattern.
factsNotEarned: Open emotional closeness between Sylvanas and Jaina.
Proof that the old carter is the same creature behind the plague.
